messages.body_plain:
Hi Steve,

I have also encountered this issue in my notes, where sometimes I want to refer to the code (was the red line really model 2?) but otherwise it can be in the way. Like you say, this is already straightforward with javascript. The implementation will depend on how the markdown parser renders html code-blocks though, so it is probably best done outside knitr, which in such a workflow just generates the markdown agnostic of how it is parsed.

I have a few examples of such javascript in my notebook; e.g. click "toggle code" on the sidebar: http://carlboettiger.info/2013/04/27/comparison-of-nonparametric-and-parametric-approaches.html

clearly a richer version could be implemented, or collapsing code blocks individually, but I haven't had time to play with it much. Anyway see the javascript <https://github.com/cboettig/labnotebook/blob/master/_includes/javascript.html> and html button <https://github.com/cboettig/labnotebook/blob/master/_includes/collapse.html> if you're interested; and thanks for sharing your thoughts.

Cheers,
Carl

>

I think it would be handy to include a javascript-powered option to embed `[ show | hide ]` links at the top (or bottom) of code chunks that you could click to alternatively hide a chunk when it is being shown, or expand a hidden chunk.

I imagine it is "easy enough" to write a post-processing script that reads in the html output from knit-ing an *.Rmd file and decorating it w/ the appropriate javascript if its too onerous to include somewhere in the Rmd -> md -> html workflow.

Hi list,

[I'm sure I saw some news about this a while ago, but google returns too many things already out-of-date with these keywords.]

I write in R + markdown, preview the html in R studio (basically knitr2html), and when I'm pleased with the output I turn to pandoc to get a slightly more fancy html output (e.g. HTML5 slides), as well as a pdf version formatted through LaTeX.

In my .rmd file, I have opts_chunk$set(dev=c('quartz_png','pdf')), so that ideally the conversion to html would pick the png images, and latex the pdf ones. It would require a bit of magic to do that, obviously, but seeing the rest already working so beautifully (even math!)...

So, my questions to you,

1- How can I get pandoc to use the pdfs instead of pngs? Using  \DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.pdf} in a tex template doesn't help, because the markdown that is coming from knit() already has hardcoded image filenames with png extension.

2- Should I stick to using pandoc from the command line, or is there now an easier integration with R? (knitr itself, pander, rapport, report, etc... -- do they offer the full functionality?)

Thanks for any insight you may have,

baptiste

For the sake of completeness, here is a straight-forward, two-step solution:

# in the rmd file, tell knitr to strip any filename extension for the included graphics
opts_knit$set('upload.fun' = function(x) sub("\\.[[:alnum:]]*$", "", x) )

# one can indeed use an internal wrapper for pandoc, recently introduced in knitr (I knew it rang a bell), and specify in a config header the appropriate option for default file extensions, e.g.

<!--pandoc
format: latex
latex-engine: xelatex
default-image-extension: pdf

format: html
default-image-extension: png
-->

and compile as,

knitr::pandoc("testing.md", "html")
knitr::pandoc("testing.md", "latex")

Sweet as!

Best regards,

baptiste
